HD.rationale: HD is a high-quality franchise under meaningful cyclical and structural pressure. Revenue grew +4.8% YoY to $41.77B in Q1 FY2026, but this is the only unambiguously positive signal. Earnings are deteriorating: EPS fell -4.3% YoY ($3.30 vs $3.45), net income declined -4.2%, and operating margin compressed 100bp to 11.9% as cost of revenue grew +6.0% — outpacing revenue growth. The margin compression is driven by acquisition integration (GMS mix impact, 75bp gross margin drag) and rising input costs (oil +30% over 90 days). ROIC has fallen from 31.3% to 25.4%, and ROE has nearly halved from 1.84× to 1.01×. The balance sheet carries ~6.8× D/E with only $13.87B equity — thin cushion against further earnings erosion. Valuation appears nominally cheap at 22.8× P/E (near 12-month lows), but this is compressing for the right reasons: the business is earning less. The earnings yield of 4.4% offers zero equity risk premium over the 10-year Treasury at 4.45%, which is rising (+40bp in 90 days). Housing turnover remains stalled, transactions are declining (-1.3% YoY), and consumer financial stress is building (47% BNPL late payments). Management reaffirmed FY2026 guidance of EPS flat-to-+4%, but RBC flagged risk of missing this on cost/demand headwinds. The structural franchise (dual DIY-Pro model, SRS distribution moat, 17% market share) is durable, but the near-term fundamental trajectory is negative with no credible near-term catalyst to reverse it. The stock is -24.8% from 52-week highs and near 52-week lows, but price decline is directionally consistent with fundamental deterioration — no mispricing exists. All three pillars align negatively: deteriorating fundamentals, no valuation discount vs. risk-adjusted basis, and no near-term re-rating catalyst.
